name: Fortuné
bio: One of the two young men at La Napoule whom Wilde called his 'two special friends' in a letter to Laurence Housman of about 28 December 1898, singling them out from the local fisher-folk. Wilde wrote that both were 'quite perfect, except that they can read and write'. No surname, age, dates or further trace appear in the letter, and nothing else about him was found in the pages read.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Laurence Housman, [Circa 28 December 1898], Hôtel des Bains, Napoule, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1113 (repo PDF 1159, printed folio 1113 confirmed at the foot of the rendered page image, read 2026-08-03). The record preserves a first name only, spelt 'Fortuné' with the acute accent on the page. Named in the same sentence as Raphael but as a separate person - 'one called Raphael, the other Fortuné' - so the two are two nodes. The letter states no age and none is inferred; it does not say either man was himself a fisherman, only that Wilde's friends were two of 'the people here - fisher-folk all'. That collective phrase names no individual and stays in the collective context_engagement on wilde.json. Full passage in dossiers/EXILE-LIAISONS_dossier.md (L4). DATES: NONE RECORDED (2026-08-03). Searched so far: the whole OCR mirror of the Complete Letters (2000) for every occurrence of the name, plus the edition's General Index; Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF, the fullest scholarly account of the exile years; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008) and Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDFs. Frankel repeats the Housman letter at printed p. 243 (repo PDF 257) and adds nothing further about either of the two men. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted, and none is likely to be: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by. That absence is itself the historical fact worth keeping - these men enter the written record only because Wilde wrote to his friends about them.
